previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of hepatic encephalopathy was admitted after presenting with right facial droop, right-sided weakness, and slurred speech, initially concerning for stroke. Imaging including CT and MRI of the brain showed no acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass. Neurological symptoms were variable and inconsistent with a focal lesion. She was diagnosed with a flare of hepatic encephalopathy, likely contributing to her neurologic presentation. Lactulose was increased to four times daily, resulting in improved mental clarity and stability of symptoms. Liver enzymes transiently elevated but trended downward, and abdominal ultrasound showed no ascites or vascular abnormalities. Blood culture showed a likely contaminant, not requiring treatment. She was discharged home with continued lactulose, instructions to avoid sedating medications, and follow-up for lab monitoring and transplant evaluation.
problems: Other, mixed, or unspecified drug abuse, unspecified

# Encephalopathy. Multifactorial, most likely medication effect 
due to oxycodone and flexeril with UTI attributing. There can 
also be a component of hepatic encephalopathy though patient did 
not have asterixis by the time she arrived on the floor. X-ray

on antiobiotics. She was discharged on multivitamin 1 tablet

# UTI. History of VRE UTI in the past. UA with 48 WBCs with 
positive nitrite. patient was started on antibiotics for 
approximately 24 hours prior to urine culture being obtained. 
Eventually urine culture was obtained which grew mixed flora.

on 7 days course of ampicillin to be completed on ___.

# ___. Due to volume depletion. Cr up to 1.2 from baseline 1.0. 
Improved after hydration. Creatinine at time of discharge 1.0.  

# Leukocytosis. Likely due to hemoconcentration as all cell 
lines up. On admission WBC 14.9 trended down to 9.3 with good PO 
intake. Over the weekend patient had decreased PO intake again 
with WBC trending up to 13.7. Infectious work up other than UTI 
negative as above including negative C. diff. Encouraged PO 
intakes and nutrition consult obtained. Needs to repeat CBC in 
___ days after discharge. 

# HCV Cirrhosis. Complicated by HE, ascites that's controlled by 
diuretics, and grade I varices. Continued Lactulose, rifaximin, 
furosemide, spironolactone, and sucralfate. Patient has multiple 
falls in the last year. Not orthostatic hypotensive this 
admission but would consider midodrine if this continues. 

# Abdominal/Back Pain: Longstanding issue, with many prior 
admission with extensive work-up (normal EGD, H.Pylori negative, 
celiac negative). Current thought is either 
constipation-predominant. Started on Amitiza 8mcg PO BID. 
Continued tylenol with minimal complaints of pain. Opioids was 
discontinued. Would not restart opioids unless absolutely 
necessary. Abdominal pain may be secondary to irritable bowel 
syndrome-constipation subtype. To treat for this, she was 
started on lubiprostone 8 mcg PO BID. She had normal bowel 
movements on this medication and did not require the use of 
opioids. Therefore in the future, opioids should be avoided as 
they may contribute to increased abdominal discomfort and 
constipation. 

# Intermittent Neurological Changes. Patient has intermittent 
right facial droop and ptosis along with weakness with left 
facial turns, left shoulder weakness, and decreased sensation on 
the left side of the face. She also has intermittent difficulty 
with word finding. She has no facial asymmetrial when she's 
alseep and symptoms seems to be worse when family is here. She 
had extensive neurological work including negative MRI/MRA 
though there is suspicion of a small vessel infarct involving 
the L thalamus, internal capsule and VPL/VPM intitially though 
given her previous waxing and waning features, they could not 
ultimately attribute her symptoms to any neurological defects. 
Her symtposm continued waxed and waned this admission and 
continue monitoring is recommended.
